raw_case_text:
A 45-year-old female patient presented with high-grade continuous fever for 5 days, headache and vomiting for 3 days, disorientation for 1-day, and facial deviation to the left side for 1-day.
On neurological examination, she had neck rigidity with positive Kernig sign. GCS Score was E3M5V4. Right-sided upper motor neuron (UMN) type facial nerve palsy was noted [Figure 3, Right panel]. Motor function, sensory function, deep tendon reflexes, cerebellar function, and autonomic function were all within normal limit. Planter was equivocal in both sides.
MRI scan of brain (plain and contrast) done on 6th day of fever, showed multiple tiny nonenhancing hypo on T1 and hyperintense lesions on T2, T2 fluid attenuation inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequence suggestive of ischemic demyelination in lentiform nucleus, peri- and para-ventricular white matter and centrum semiovale on both sides [Figure 3, Left panel]. So, a diagnosis of dengue meningoencephalitis with right sided UMN type facial palsy was made.
The patient was treated with intravenous (IV) fluid and antipyretics, and at the end of the 2nd week patient became completely afebrile with no neck rigidity but facial palsy persisted partially. Patient was discharged and on follow-up at the end of the 4th week there was complete resolution of facial palsy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 45-year-old female presented with high-grade continuous fever for 5 days, headache and vomiting for 3 days, and disorientation and leftward facial deviation for 1 day.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced 5 days of continuous high-grade fever, followed by 3 days of headache and vomiting, and 1 day of acute disorientation and left-sided facial deviation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for continuous high-grade fever, headache, vomiting, disorientation, and facial asymmetry.

objective.physical_examination: GCS E3M5V4, neck rigidity, positive Kernig sign, and right-sided upper motor neuron (UMN) facial nerve palsy; motor, sensory, deep tendon reflex, cerebellar, and autonomic examinations were normal with bilateral equivocal plantar responses.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI (plain and contrast) on day 6 of fever revealed multiple tiny non-enhancing T1-hypointense and T2/FLAIR-hyperintense lesions in the bilateral lentiform nuclei, periventricular/paraventricular white matter, and centrum semiovale suggestive of ischemic demyelination.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Dengue meningoencephalitis complicated by right upper motor neuron facial nerve palsy and subcortical ischemic demyelination on brain MRI. Treated conservatively with intravenous fluids and antipyretics, achieving complete defervescence and resolution of neck rigidity by week 2 and full recovery of facial nerve palsy at 4-week follow-up.
